source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 68: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions: this is collective-initialization scenario variant 68. Backend, launcher, versions, expected world size, host placement, scheduler, container permissions, fabric, selected interfaces, topology, and the exact blocked stage are unknown; measure them rather than infer them. Run only in an isolated authorized allocation, redact endpoints and credentials, set a bounded watchdog, and guarantee process cleanup. Capture a run ID, host/rank/local-rank/world size, PID, configuration and software hashes, rendezvous/store endpoints and membership, collective entry/exit timestamps, last-progress events, stderr, transport diagnostics, and GPU/NIC identifiers. Verify that every expected rank starts exactly once, membership and endpoint agree, all ranks enter collectives in identical order, GPU visibility and rank-to-device mapping are unique, driver/runtime/backend compatibility holds, peer access and PCIe/NVLink topology are healthy, and the container, shared memory, ulimits, NIC/address/route/DNS/MTU/firewall settings are usable.

Falsifiable hypothesis: a rank-specific rendezvous membership or selected transport path defect prevents all participants from entering the same collective. Support it only if repeated trials show the same rank/path-specific missing or late membership, failed connection, or transport error and a single authorized membership/interface correction restores progress; reject it if synchronized membership and transport evidence are clean while an alternate cause reproduces the hang.

Controlled experiment: first record a baseline with a tiny checksum-verified all-reduce and a bounded timeout. Randomize repeated, matched trials across single-node, reduced-world, and full-world allocations while holding code, data, seed, message size, rank mapping, and timeout fixed; change only one authorized factor per arm (rendezvous/interface/backend/topology) and include a blocked control. Record per-rank entry/exit and timeout/error outcomes, latency, checksum correctness, and cleanup success with denominators. Compare failure rates and rank/path signatures, not anecdotes; inspect collective-order divergence, GPU/runtime errors, resource exhaustion, topology/rail choice, firewall/MTU, store availability, and software/configuration differences as confounders.

Safety and decision gates: stop on repeated timeout, corruption, unexplained rank loss, or watchdog breach; do not extend timeouts to hide a fault or change production networking without approval. Preserve redacted logs and configuration hashes, terminate orphaned processes, and roll back any diagnostic interface/backend change. Treat reduced-world success as insufficient for full-world sign-off; require repeated full-world correctness, bounded latency, no unexplained failures, and expert review before claiming resolution.
risks: The hang may instead be caused by collective-order divergence, GPU/device/runtime faults, resource limits, or intermittent infrastructure.
Single-node or reduced-world success does not establish full-world network correctness; limited trials can miss rare failures.
Interface or backend changes and retries can affect traffic unless isolated, authorized, and bounded.
evidence_required: Redacted per-rank rendezvous and collective timelines; membership and rank-to-device mapping; topology, GPU, driver/runtime, NIC, route, and transport diagnostics; repeated randomized matched trials with checksums; separate outcome denominators and configuration hashes.

Controlled experiment: first record a baseline with a tiny checksum-verified all-reduce and a bounded timeout. Randomize repeated, matched trials across single-node, reduced-world, and full-world allocations while holding code, data, seed, message size, rank mapping, and timeout fixed; change only one authorized factor per arm (rendezvous/interface/backend/topology) and include a blocked control. Record per-rank entry/exit and timeout/error outcomes, latency, checksum correctness, and cleanup success with denominators. Compare failure rates and rank/path signatures, not anecdotes; inspect collective-order divergence, GPU/runtime errors, resource exhaustion, topology/rail choice, firewall/MTU, store availability, and software/configuration differences as confounders.

Safety and decision gates: stop on repeated timeout, corruption, unexplained rank loss, or watchdog breach; do not extend timeouts to hide a fault or change production networking without approval. Preserve redacted logs and configuration hashes, terminate orphaned processes, and roll back any diagnostic interface/backend change. Treat reduced-world success as insufficient for full-world sign-off; require repeated full-world correctness, bounded latency, no unexplained failures, and expert review before claiming resolution.
risks: The hang may instead be caused by collective-order divergence, GPU/device/runtime faults, resource limits, or intermittent infrastructure.
Single-node or reduced-world success does not establish full-world network correctness; limited trials can miss rare failures.
Interface or backend changes and retries can affect traffic unless isolated, authorized, and bounded.
evidence_required: Redacted per-rank rendezvous and collective timelines; membership and rank-to-device mapping; topology, GPU, driver/runtime, NIC, route, and transport diagnostics; repeated randomized matched trials with checksums; separate outcome denominators and configuration hashes.
